newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest receives rain, cool weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest receives rain, cool weather forecast.

text.p: Rain from the remnants of Hurricane Fran remained east of the U.S. Midwest crop areas, but by Sunday a separate storm system moving east brought rain to much of the Midwest, meteorologists said.
Also, meteorologists said the Midwest will turn cool this week with low temperatures in the 40s (degrees Fahrenheit).
Copious amounts of rain from Fran fell from North Carolina north to Pennsylvania and west into eastern Ohio.
"All of the heavy rain (from Fran) fell in the eastern sections of Ohio and there are not a whole lot of crops there," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.

A cold front that entered the Midwest this past weekend brought 0.25 to 1.25 inch of rain to the western Midwest Saturday and early Sunday and 0.30 to 0.90 inch to the eastern Midwest Sunday, said Burgio.
Meteorologists said the rain was beneficial to the dry crop areas in the eastern Midwest, but more is needed.
"A bit more moisture would have been welcome in the east, but at least Monday's rain event will be a small shot in the arm for the region," said Basilia Lopez, Smith Barney meteorologist.

Beginning Tuesday the Midwest should turn cool with temperatures averaging five to 10 degrees below normal by late this week, said Burgio. Lows should range from near 40 degrees in Minnesota and Wisconsin to the 50s elsewhere.
No frost is forecast for the week, but Burgio said there is a slight chance for frost in Minnesota and Wisconsin. The cool weather should extend into next week.
"It does look like we are setting up a below-normal (temperature) pattern for the Midwest," said Burgio.
